title: From mukaish to antique tilla, Sharvari’s lehenga brought together a mix of heritage crafts and colours

 Open Navigation Menu Menu Trends From mukaish to antique tilla, Sharvari’s lehenga brought together a mix of heritage crafts and colours
 The actor's lehenga from designer Iqbal Hussain was a culmination of over 1,500 hours of intricate handiwork By Nupur Sarvaiya 21 November 2026 Instagram.com/sharvari Sharvari is making the most of her promotions for her upcoming movie Yeh Prem Mol Liya to showcase the versatility of traditional occasion wear. From classic weaves to statement silhouettes, she’s been serving looks worth taking notes. This time around, she turned to South Asian designer Iqbal Hussain for a lehenga with an interplay of vibrant hues, intricate handwork, and heritage textiles.
 The lehenga brings tangerine and forest green—an unusual colour combination—together on pure raw silk textile. “The two colours meet in carefully constructed panels, and feel both festive and refreshingly modern,” shares Hussain.
 Instagram.com/sharvari
 Up close, the craft does the talking. There are delicate sequin-embellished threadwork bootis scattered across the lehenga, while the tiered borders feature bands of fine mukaish, classic marodi and antique tilla work. A thick tier of mustard-yellow jamawar textile adds to its old-world charm.
 The blouse is a deep V-neck sequin-embellished creation in vivid pink with contrasting olive elbow-length sleeves, embroidered with thread and tilla work, finished with marodi and mukaish borders. Completing the look is a hot pink tulle dupatta, edged with matching embroidery techniques, scattered with mukaish-worked motifs throughout. According to Hussain, the ensemble represents approximately 1,500 hours of meticulous craftsmanship.
 Instagram.com/sharvari
 Sharvari took a maximalist approach with accessorising her lehenga. She chose a kundan set statement necklace centred on chand motifs and intricate Meenakari detailing. She paired it with elaborate jhumkas, complemented by a kaan phool, an ornate haath phool, rings and a statement bracelet. With her hair worn loose in soft waves and makeup in soft tones, she let the focus remain on the lehenga.
 Sharvari’s promotional looks are an inspiration for wedding guests and brides seeking ideas for dressing up this wedding season. Earlier this month, the actor rewore her mother’s patola sari with a purple jamawar corset , perfect for a cocktail or a reception party. She also wore yet another patola lehenga from Torani, which would turn heads at a haldi or a mehendi ceremony. This lehenga, too, is designed for the wedding calendar, with dholkis, mehndis and sangeets in mind.
